text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- Nearly 2,000 students or 15 percent too many in terms of capacity have signed up for medical studies at universities in Switzerland, seven percent more than in 1996.
- New York cancelled its call to boycott Swiss banks after the Swiss government approved the creation of a special fund for Holocaust victims.
- Roche sold Rolic, its liquid crystals business to Swiss entrepreneur Karl Nicklaus.
- U.S. chemical firm Witco Corporation is setting up its headquarters for Europe, Africa and the Middle East in Geneva.
- Edwin Somm, director of ABB Schweiz, will join ABB's board of directors.
- Two dozen new automobiles not yet seen by the public will be among the highlights shown at the Geneva Automobile Show from Martch 6 to 16. More than 600,000 visitors are expected to attend.
- The number of workers employed in the Swiss building industry fell below 100,000 for the first time since 1983 and is now around 96,000.
- The Sarasin Group posted a 17.2 percent increase in operating results to 154 million Swiss francs in 1996. Profit rose by 15.7 percent to 34.2 million Swiss francs.
- Despite 16 percent growth in 1996, ABB expects neither increased turnover nor higher profit for 1997.
